title: VISION-LANGUAGE MODELS GENERATE MORE HOMOGENEOUS STORIES FOR PHENOTYPICALLY BLACK INDIVIDUALS

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting Vision-Language Models with computer-generated facial images of Black individuals that systematically vary in racial phenotypicality, and evaluating content homogeneity by calculating the cosine similarity of sentence embeddings from the generated stories.
Measuring and comparing the semantic homogeneity of VLM-generated stories prompted by images of Black women versus Black men using the cosine similarity of their sentence embeddings.
Analyzing the interaction effect between gender and racial phenotypicality to determine if the impact of phenotypicality on story homogeneity differs significantly between Black women and Black men.
